signature: SUBROUTINE ZGGSVP3( JOBU, JOBV, JOBQ, M, P, N, A, LDA, B, LDB,

params.name: jobu
params.reference:
-   `= 'U'`: Unitary matrix U is computed;
-   `= 'N'`: U is not computed.

params.name: jobv
params.reference:
-   `= 'V'`: Unitary matrix V is computed;
-   `= 'N'`: V is not computed.

params.name: jobq
params.reference:
-   `= 'Q'`: Unitary matrix Q is computed;
-   `= 'N'`: Q is not computed.

params.name: M
params.reference: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.

params.name: P
params.reference: The number of rows of the matrix B. $P \ge 0$.

params.name: N
params.reference: The number of columns of the matrices A and B. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the M-by-N matrix A. On exit, A contains the triangular (or trapezoidal) matrix described in the Purpose section.
params.workDependent: the triangular reduction of A depends on ZGEQP3's pivot order, which LWORK's block size can change in near ties

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,M)$.

params.name: B
params.reference: On entry, the P-by-N matrix B. On exit, B contains the triangular matrix described in the Purpose section.
params.workDependent: the triangular reduction of B depends on ZGEQP3's pivot order, which LWORK's block size can change in near ties

params.name: ldb
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array B. $\mathrm{LDB} \ge \max (1,P)$.

params.name: tolb
params.reference:
`TOLA` and `TOLB` are the thresholds to determine the effective numerical rank of matrix B and a subblock of A. Generally, they are set to

$$
\mathrm{TOLA} = \max (M,N) \, \operatorname{norm}(A) \, \mathrm{MAZHEPS}
$$

$$
\mathrm{TOLB} = \max (P,N) \, \operatorname{norm}(B) \, \mathrm{MAZHEPS}
$$

The size of `TOLA` and `TOLB` may affect the size of backward errors of the decomposition.

params.name: l
params.reference: On exit, K and L specify the dimension of the subblocks described in Purpose section. K + L = effective numerical rank of $(A^H,B^H)^H$.

params.name: U
params.reference: If `JOBU = 'U'`, U contains the unitary matrix U. If `JOBU = 'N'`, U is not referenced.
params.workDependent: U follows the pivot order that LWORK's block size can change

params.name: ldu
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array U. $\mathrm{LDU} \ge \max (1,M)$ if `JOBU = 'U'`; $\mathrm{LDU} \ge 1$ otherwise.

params.name: V
params.reference: If `JOBV = 'V'`, V contains the unitary matrix V. If `JOBV = 'N'`, V is not referenced.
params.workDependent: V follows the pivot order that LWORK's block size can change

params.name: ldv
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array V. $\mathrm{LDV} \ge \max (1,P)$ if `JOBV = 'V'`; $\mathrm{LDV} \ge 1$ otherwise.

params.name: Q
params.reference: If `JOBQ = 'Q'`, Q contains the unitary matrix Q. If `JOBQ = 'N'`, Q is not referenced.
params.workDependent: Q follows the pivot order that LWORK's block size can change

params.name: ldq
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array Q. $\mathrm{LDQ} \ge \max (1,N)$ if `JOBQ = 'Q'`; $\mathrm{LDQ} \ge 1$ otherwise.

params.name: IWORK
params.workDependent: the pivots LWORK's block size can change in near ties

params.name: TAU
params.workDependent: scratch reflector scalars of the pivoted factorizations

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.

notes: check INFO=-24 tests LWORK, not argument 24 (WORK): the reference misnumbers it

overrides.reason: ZGGSVP3 hands its LWORK to ZGEQP3, which picks its block size from LWORK and falls back to the unblocked ZLAQP2 when the workspace is short of (N+1)*NB. The blocked and unblocked column-pivoted QR update the column norms differently, so where two candidate columns are nearly tied they can pivot differently, and A, B, U, V, Q (and the pivots in IWORK) then hold a different, equally valid reduction U^H*A*Q, V^H*B*Q. K and L do not depend on LWORK; the module's tests check the reduction at the minimum WORK past the blocking threshold by residual (ticket 0100).
